explanation: Espresso is far stronger per sip, but a single shot holds only about 30 ml. A mug of filter coffee is about eight times bigger, so it usually delivers more caffeine overall.

claims.text: A single 30 ml shot of espresso typically contains about 63 mg of caffeine.
A 240 ml serving of brewed filter coffee typically contains about 95 mg of caffeine.
Espresso contains more caffeine per millilitre than filter coffee.
A 240 ml mug holds about eight times the volume of a 30 ml espresso shot.

writerNotes: Self-check (CONTENT_GUIDE 9.3). Lint: content:check run on the batch until this item showed no errors. Claims: every checkable statement is listed; risk is at or above the C26 floor (high: c1, c2, c4). The item is counterintuitive, so its key claim (both label claims, for a comparison) is high under the C26 floor; where no other reason applies, checker_doubt stands in for the guide's 'counterintuitive', which the schema's riskReason enum lacks. Datasets: No pinned dataset covers this food fact (the manifest holds countries, cities, elements, languages, currencies, Nobel Prizes, World Cups, Olympic Games and artists), so the claims rest on checker knowledge, with external evidence needed for the high-risk ones. Rival test: Caffeine varies a lot by bean and barista, so the stem says 'usually' and the values are typical figures from food-composition tables; a double shot or a tiny mug could flip it, which is why the labels say single shot and mug. The strength of espresso is the trap. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: both drinks are sold worldwide. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens, single quotation marks, explanation of 32 words. Myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches any claim. Mystery and encore checks: not applicable to a practice item. Seed: 5: most players pick the espresso. Doubts: the variation in real servings is the main risk; the typical values put filter coffee about 50% ahead, comfortably past the 1.1 guard.
